brief_rationale: The doctor completed all responsibility-chain items without serious error, including active reconciliation of patient information, red-flag screening, safe result interpretation boundaries, medication safety, glucose context, concrete follow-up plan, and handoff receipt. Two high-order points were completed: HO3 (safe bounded closure with explicit residual uncertainties) and HO4 (false-positive/negative verification by distinguishing order items from completed reports). HO1 and HO2 were not triggered because the hidden context was discovered through routine RC1 reconciliation and no patient misconception was stated. The trajectory achieves grade 5 (Perfect) with safe, executable, traceable closure and two completed high-order points.

high_order_assessment.explanation: The hidden context (diagnosis, medications, follow-up instructions, glucose-tolerance abnormality) was discovered through routine RC1 reconciliation via workspace queries and patient dialogue. The doctor did not proactively uncover additional non-volunteered facts beyond what was required for minimum RC1-RC4 duties. The facts were used but not in a beyond-minimum discovery manner that would qualify for HO1 credit.

No patient misconception was stated or implied in the trajectory. The patient asked clarifying questions but did not express false beliefs about nasal endoscopy proving tumor recurrence, IGF-1 being a diabetes test, or octreotide being a casual anti-inflammatory. HO2 was not triggered.
